description: Match a plain-language need (e.g. "cheapest AI app builder with a free plan", "terminal coding agent under $25") to tools in the catalogue. How it ranks: Keyword match over the catalogue, no model involved. 1) Words in the request set filters: "app builder"/"no-code"/"no code" -> type App Builder; "ide"/"editor" -> AI IDE; "terminal"/"cli" -> Terminal Agent; "free" -> only tools with a free plan; "under $N"/"below $N"/"less than $N" -> starting price at most $N; "beginner"/"non-coder"/"non-technical" -> skill level Beginner. 2) Remaining tools are scored by how many other request words appear in the name, bestFor, features and type. 3) Order: if the request says cheap/cheapest/budget/affordable, lowest starting price first; otherwise highest match score, then claw.mobile rating (unrated last), then lowest starting price. Starting price is the first dollar figure the vendor lists, which may be an annual-billing rate or per user. The response repeats the filters it read from the request.

need.description: What the person wants, in their words
